newsitem.title: QATAR: Jordan offers Qatar stake in gas project.
newsitem.headline: Jordan offers Qatar stake in gas project.

text.p: Jordan said on Monday it has offered the Gulf Arab state Qatar a partnership in a proposed $300 million gas plant that would be built in Jordan to supply gas to Jordanian and regional markets.

"We discussed this offer with...the Emir and the minister of energy and industry (of Qatar), but I am not aware of how much stake they will take", Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali told a news conference on a visit to Doha.
There was no official word from oil- and gas-rich Qatar on whether it would accept the Jordanian offer to boost its role from that of gas supplier in the Aqaba project to partner.

Jordan's Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Mohammad al-Hourani, accompanying the prime minister, told Reuters: "The US company, Enron Corp, is also involved in the project and discussions with it are progressing".

Enron had spearheaded the project to set up the regasification plant at Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba, to bring liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Qatar to Israel and Jordan in the first quarter of 2001.
Israel pulled out of the deal, agreed two years ago amid a wave of optimism about Arab-Israeli economic cooperation.
Majali stressed the project had not been shelved.

Hourani said Jordan would take 500,000 tonnes a year of LNG and the remaining two million tonnes, which Enron would import from Qatar, could be supplied to Palestinian self-ruled areas and other parts of the region.
